title: Local dev-mode is never authoritative for ship coverage
iWant: the ship gate to refuse a deployed-scope AC bound to a dev-mode probe
soThat: no emulator drift can pass for a real runtime signal

acceptanceCriteria.description: A test case whose runtime probe hits the local dev-mode URL (matching the pattern for the vendor's local emulator, for example `http://localhost:8787` or the `wrangler dev` bound port) is refused as coverage for any AC whose `scope` is `deployed`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an AC with `scope: 'deployed'` bound to a TC whose runtime target URL matches the dev-mode pattern
acceptanceCriteria.when: the coverage gate walks the AC-to-TC bindings
acceptanceCriteria.then: the gate reports the binding as `DEPLOY_DEV_MODE_INADMISSIBLE`, refuses to count it toward the AC's coverage, and lists the offending TC and its target URL

acceptanceCriteria.description: A probe against a preview alias URL, a version-id URL, or the production URL is accepted as coverage for a deployed-scope AC.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an AC with `scope: 'deployed'` bound to a TC whose runtime target URL matches the vendor's preview or production URL patterns
acceptanceCriteria.when: the coverage gate walks the AC-to-TC bindings
acceptanceCriteria.then: the gate accepts the binding as valid coverage; the coverage counter increments for the AC

acceptanceCriteria.description: The project's runtime-verify catalogue documents the dev-mode drift classes (regular-expression engine differences, static-assets ordering differences, binding-emulation differences, timeout behaviour) so an engineer authoring a probe knows which behaviours cannot be trusted at the local surface.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the file names at least four dev-mode drift classes with a one-line example of each and a pointer to the vendor's changelog or release notes where the class is described
